main_text.p: χαειτων ὢ παιδεία τοῖς χρωμένοις, ἓ ἀν ὃν ἐπισρέψη, Διόσωσιόπλαυ Interdum junguntur,ut synonyma, תשלר ו צלח & ת שלר ה ut Josh. c. I. verf. 8. כי אז תצליח את דרכך ואז תשכיל quod Junius, Tunc enim prosperaberis in viis tuis, & tunc secundaberis. Anglica; For then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good successe. appositâ tamen ibi ad oram & altera verbi significatione, [or, Doe wiselp :] ut Lectori liberum esset, quam mallet ipse, amplecti. quod & alibi saepius in istâ versione observatur, ut altera in textu, altera in adversâ orâ significatio Lectori, quasi in dubiâ re, proponatur; vel fortasse, quasi in utrâque aliquid ad sententiam aut pleniorem sensum momenti esset, commendetur. Ita certè, Josuae c. I. v.7, & 8. I.Sam.XVIII. v. 5, & 14. sed & in nomine, ab eodem verbo, substantivo, Proverb. cap. III. verf. 4. & Psal. CXI. verfu ultimo.
Hinc autem ansa sive discendi, sive meditandi, quod non unus veterum pro magno sapientiae arcano vendita-vit. fua quemque fortuna (ut apud Salustium Appius) fabrum esse: vel, suos cuiq;

page.notes: Hebrew and Greek lines are reproduced as far as legible; Hebrew and Greek readings are approximate. The bracketed English gloss "Doe wiselp" is as printed and may be damaged. Catchword "cuiq;" appears at the foot right and is given at the end of the text paragraph.
